summary: The board-specific logic is a single gfx state machine. Once per frame it draws the whole 256x256 tilemap into a double-buffered frame buffer, then blits the 32 sprites in the same order, with the same field decoding and the same 240-sy transform as MAME's screen_update_chameleo/draw_sprites. Nothing is tied to a pixel clock or raster counters: the tilemap/sprite passes run free of the video timing, and a separate generic video module scans the frame buffer out. Address decode and the I/O register case statements follow MAME's address map and handlers (including the sound_select bitswap). Nothing in the code reflects board chips, counters or signal names.

findings.signal: per-frame batch render into frame buffer
findings.note: gfx walks every tile pixel (states 0-3), then every sprite pixel (states 8-10), and writes each one to a double-buffered 256x256 vram swapped on 'frame'. That is MAME's bitmap fill + tilemap draw + draw_sprites order, not a scan-time pipeline.
spr_addr starts at 31 and counts down to 0, which matches MAME's reverse=0 walk from the end of spriteram with inc=-4. Each sprite is drawn as a nested 16x16 px/py loop, like gfx->transpen.

findings.signal: identical sprite field decode and coordinate math
findings.note: sx=byte3, sy=240-byte0, code=byte1&0x3f with gfxbank<<6, flipx=byte1 bit6, flipy=byte1 bit7, color=byte2&0x0f: the same expressions MAME uses, including its '240 - sy'.
A sprite pixel is written only when the looked-up colour is non-zero, an overwrite into the bitmap like MAME's transpen. There is no line-buffer or priority logic of the kind a board would have.

The code is read from videoram (0x400 region), then the colour from colorram (0x800 region), forming {bank,code} and color&0x0f, as in the tile_info callback (code | gfxbank<<8, color & 0x0f). The fetch is sequenced by the state machine, not by H/V counter bits.
Flip is applied at the frame-buffer write address (256-hh / 256-vv), like MAME's set_flip_all on the rendered bitmap, rather than by inverting counter bits.

findings.signal: I/O handlers follow MAME address map
findings.note: The case statements on addr[2:0] reproduce map entries 0x1800-0x1807 and 0xb000-0xb005 one for one. The SN data is bit-reversed exactly like MAME's bitswap<8>(...,0,1,...,7).
The NMI fires on a change in the coin bits and the audio IRQ on any change of snd_latch value, mirroring MAME's INPUT_CHANGED and latch-pending callbacks rather than a board latch/flip-flop.
A black final RGB is replaced by the back_color register, an approximation of MAME's pen-0 override, applied after the palette lookup.

findings.signal: generic video timing and clock enables
findings.note: Raster timing is a generic hcount/vcount generator that only scans the frame buffer out. Clock enables come from clk_sys. Both are FPGA plumbing, unrelated to the board.
The chip-select decode and ROM placement match the CPU memory maps, which any correct implementation must share.
